heading: A size advantage in heading persistence can coexist with multiple active regions.
overall_interpretation: H1 is inconclusive, H2 fails the declared overall gate and H3 is inconclusive in both arms and all seven views, with forced states shown separately. No model satisfies all H1 requirements (three required); only Holmes meets the main H2 model criterion (two required). The multiple-region predictor has Spearman +0.091 and 0/4 successful sign folds; count has−0.389 and 3/4, with one unavailable fold each. Neither reaches the required negative association magnitude 0.6. No eligible distinct H3 mode pair satisfies the complete corroboration/fingerprint conjunction. The chosen main figure instead reports the robust f = 0.05 observation in Wave-pinning, Holmes and Spring, with the full four-model overview alongside it. This is a conditional polarity result, not support for universal noise buffering or a validated multiplicity predictor.
retained_qualifications: Finite-window bounds, unavailable comparisons and unbounded intervals remain explicit. Across all 185 conditions, each arm has 156 passing,17 failing and 12 inconclusive descriptive window checks. For the 52 preselected extended conditions, each view has 50 passing and 2 inconclusive horizon checks; the original-cohort check has the same counts. These are sensitivity qualifications, not additional hypothesis gates or equivalence proofs. At the selected input, all three-model size-ratio CIs remain above 1 in all seven views; selected endpoint persistence/regime window checks pass. Native regimes and fixed-physical smoothed/downsampled imaging proxies stay distinct. Global-heading physical mobility is a proxy, literal single-region site MSD is separate, and neither establishes cell migration. Historical Spring sampling failures and original/repaired/E4 Gaussian-lineage accounting remain in the supplement. The selected f = 0.05 conditions were not preselected for E4 extension. Both selector tables reuse the same common-horizon observations here; they are one cohort, rather than independent long-horizon confirmation.
